Putting together is super easy and the while the mower doesn’t seem like its built for rugged terrain it will be serviceable and stand up for many years i believe.   We shall see. title: Wild Badger Power 40 Volt Self-Propelled Mower
text:
Why I Tried This Mower
I wanted to see if the Wild Badger Power 40 Volt Self-Propelled Lawn Mower could handle my 1/2-acre lot during the fall. Between grass clippings and leaves, I needed something quiet and cordless to make the job easier.

My Experience
Putting the mower together was quick and easy—no hassles there. It’s lightweight and really easy to move around, but I did notice the plastic wheels slipping on slight inclines, which got annoying. When I used the bagging option, the bag only filled to about 75% before I had to stop and empty it, which slowed things down. Plus, the batteries ran out before I could finish the job, and recharging them took longer than I expected.

When I switched to mulching, things went way smoother. It handled the mix of grass and leaves well, and I was able to finish the whole yard with both batteries.

What It Did for Me
The mower was super quiet, which was great—I didn’t feel like I was disturbing anyone. Mulching saved me time since I didn’t have to keep stopping to empty the bag. On the downside, the battery life isn’t quite enough for my yard when bagging, and the long charging time was frustrating.

My Take
This mower is a good fit for smaller, flat yards. It’s easy to use, does a great job mulching, and is lightweight. But for larger yards or places with inclines, the battery life, recharge time, and wheel traction might be a problem.

Overall, it’s a nice eco-friendly option, but it comes with a few trade-offs if you’ve got a bigger yard like mine.

title: Good but for small yards
text: Lowe’s sent me this product for review in December of 2024 and since my lawn was dormant i decided that scalping a lawn with this mower would be the ultimate test.  I don’t go down all the way to the roots but i do like to clean it up so the new grass can gain exposure to the sun.   My honest opinion is this is a good strong mower but the battery life would only get you through a very small yard at best, unless you already own more 20volt “badger” batteries.   Now i do live on a little more than half an acre and didn’t expect to mow the entire lot with this mower but i kept hoping it would surprise me.   I charged both batteries fully thinking i could use one then charge that one while i used the other one.  My mistake as it requires both batteries to operate.   While i mowed the mower was fabulous.   It only bogged down on things that i would expect it to.  Keep in mind im mowing on the lowest height setting for this mower.   While i will keep the mower (thanks Lowe’s) it will be for a strip i have on my lawn that my riding mower cannot get into.   It will replace a 21 year old mower and i have faith it will do the job just fine.   Keeping up the batteries will be the hardest part as i don’t have much use for them outside of this.   Putting together is super easy and the while the mower doesn’t seem like its built for rugged terrain it will be serviceable and stand up for many years i believe.   We shall see.   As far as battery usefullness it simply is for a small yard without many obstacles.   I mowed these two areas with one charge.  Keep in mind i live on a little more than half an acre so these seem like small areas and they are compared to the rest of the yard but i thought it was decent compared to how short i was mowing.

title: Wild Badger Power 40 Volt Self-Propelled Mower
text:
Why I Tried This Mower
I wanted to see if the Wild Badger Power 40 Volt Self-Propelled Lawn Mower could handle my 1/2-acre lot during the fall. Between grass clippings and leaves, I needed something quiet and cordless to make the job easier.

My Experience
Putting the mower together was quick and easy—no hassles there. It’s lightweight and really easy to move around, but I did notice the plastic wheels slipping on slight inclines, which got annoying. When I used the bagging option, the bag only filled to about 75% before I had to stop and empty it, which slowed things down. Plus, the batteries ran out before I could finish the job, and recharging them took longer than I expected.

When I switched to mulching, things went way smoother. It handled the mix of grass and leaves well, and I was able to finish the whole yard with both batteries.

What It Did for Me
The mower was super quiet, which was great—I didn’t feel like I was disturbing anyone. Mulching saved me time since I didn’t have to keep stopping to empty the bag. On the downside, the battery life isn’t quite enough for my yard when bagging, and the long charging time was frustrating.

My Take
This mower is a good fit for smaller, flat yards. It’s easy to use, does a great job mulching, and is lightweight. But for larger yards or places with inclines, the battery life, recharge time, and wheel traction might be a problem.

Overall, it’s a nice eco-friendly option, but it comes with a few trade-offs if you’ve got a bigger yard like mine.

title: Not bad, could be better
text:
I can't really say how well this mower performs cutting grass, since it was sent to me in December & there's no real grass to cut here in Ohio. I will submit another review in spring about performance. 
The mower was easy to assemble. Only requiring the handle to be installed and charge the battery. 
Positives: Light weight & quiet. Easy to handle, nice bag attachment. Multiple handle adjustments are a nice touch, as is the 1 lever height adjustment and the carrying handle at the motor. This will be perfect for the yard at my campsite.
Not so positive: Poorly thought out design.
Mulch plate could have been built into the chute cover, rather than having a separate piece that must be removed & could easily be misplaced. Safety swich not great. I understand safety devices are necessary, but the button on the side is awkward and inconvenient in my opinion. A small lever closer to the top for the thumb to press would have been sufficiently safe. The clips included to secure the wire harness work poorly and the cable flops around. The wheels are cheap, hard plastic and I don't see them lasting very long. I also feel 2 batteries should have been included.
Overall this mower will be decent for a smaller, flat yard. I would recommend it for that purpose only.

title: Mixed emotions
text:
Rough one/mixed emotions...
Originally I purchased this item, because the previous mower I owned. Would shut off due to the grass being so thick. This mower definitely did not turn off during mowing the grass. So that is a plus. However the mower feels so weak. It's made mostly of plastic. The blade and handle are the only metal pieces on this mower. It doesn't seem very durable. I don't know how long it would last after being vigorously used. The battery does last quite a while. I ran it for over an hour, and it was still half charged. One big complaint I have is that it does not come with assembly instructions. It was simple enough to figure out without it, but if you are not mechanically inclined, this could be an issue. It does come with everything you need to begin mowing, battery, charger, mulching attachment, collecting bag etc.
If you have a very small lawn, and are mechanically inclined. this item would be perfect for you.
If you have a large lawn and, are not familiar with assembling items, I do not recommend this mower.
All in all it successfully mowed my lawn, with no stoppages. However again this mower does not feel very durable, or sturdy.

productName: 52 cc Gas 2-Stroke 2-in-1 Brush Cutter and String Hand Held Trimmer
title: DO NOT PURCHASE!
text:
I ordered this online from Home Depot. Home Depot is great! Fast delivery. However: THIS PRODUCT IS TERRIBLE! Upon delivery, I couldn’t assemble it properly due to terrible instructions included that actually show a part THAT DOES NOT EVEN EXIST and if it did would make the unit unusable! I had to go on YouTube for an assembly video. Upon completion, it ran for about ten minutes and the trimmer line broke TWICE while trimming just grass! I am familiar with trimmers, avoid hitting the fence and other objects, and I have used them for many years. I’m not a rookie! Respooling the line was not too difficult but two line failures in ten minutes is not acceptable! The vibrations are excessive! So excessive that the spring loaded pin that positions the lower shaft into the upper shaft is shaken out of its position causing the trimmer head to rotate clockwise out of position despite the hand screw designed to hold the shaft in position (along with the spring loaded pin) being tightened very tight. After several re-assemblies of the lower shaft for this issue, I called Wild Badger customer support and was asked to re-assemble it again for the agent. It failed again. I had to send pictures and was told that a new unit would be sent. It never arrived. The new unit was actually delivered to a different state and different address according to the tracking information. Wild Badger says that the unit is not returnable to them or to Home Depot! Not true! After the new unit did not arrive, a call to Home Depot appeared to solve the issue. They said to drain the gasoline and return it to the store and they would send a new unit with a courtesy discount. Like I said, Home Depot is great!!! The new unit arrived, was assembled, started easily, and worked FOR LESS THAN TEN MINUTES before the same issues started again. Thinking I may have done something wrong, I watched a different YouTube assembly video and re-assembled the unit. (I actually hadn’t done anything incorrectly with the assembly of either unit!) Upon starting it again, the same line break and head rotation occurred. JUST DON’T BUY THIS MACHINE! 
I will be returning this unit to Home Depot today and selecting a different brand.
